title: ctxpipe check manifest
description: Output of `pnpm checks:list`. A reader rejects an unknown schemaVersion. A new optional property does not change the version.

id.description: `<family>:<lane>:<file>`, or `<family>:<lane>:<file>#<case>` for one case of a file (a Storybook story, an eval case). A file id is a prefix of the ids of its cases.

family.description: `vitest`: a Vitest test file. `storybook`: a Storybook story with a play function, played in Chromium. `eval`: an eval case that calls paid models. `typecheck`: one TypeScript project. `lint`: oxlint, oxfmt or knip over the repo. `policy`: a policy script of the CI lint job, or the Terraform plan. `build`: one production image or one package build of the CI build jobs.

lane.description: One group of checks that run together: for Vitest one runner invocation (package directory, config and runtime); for other families the kind of check.

root.description: Repo-relative directory that holds the check (`""` is the repo root). A changed file below it, that no check imports and that is not code, selects the whole lane.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file that defines the check: the test file, the stories file, the eval cases or scenario, the tsconfig, or the lint config or policy script.

inputs.description: Repo-relative paths that are not imported by the check but change its result: configs, setup files, the lockfile, the runner, and the source of built code that the check runs. A path that ends in `/**` stands for a whole directory. A change to one selects the whole lane. For the `typecheck`, `lint` and `policy` families, the inputs are the directories that the check reads, approximated.

traceInputs.description: Inputs (each also in `inputs`) for which a reader with a trace (trace.v1.schema.json) may select checks from the trace instead of the whole lane. `lines`: the input is source that the checks run in Node child processes; the trace records those lines when the check's `recorded` holds `children`, so a changed file selects as any traced source file does. `tables`: the input holds Drizzle migration directories. A changed `migration.sql` selects the checks whose cases touched a table that a changed statement names (the case property `tables`) and the checks that read the file (`reads`, or `dirs` of a directory above it). Any other changed file in the input selects the checks that read it; `snapshot.json` is drizzle-kit state that no check reads. The input selects the whole lane when the trace does not hold the needed kind for the lane's checks, or when the reader cannot name the tables of a changed statement.

runtime.description: The runtime that runs the lane. A result cache adds its version to the key.

env.description: The environment variables that change the result of the lane. Optional; without it, no variable.

mode.description: `value`: a result cache adds a hash of the value to the key; the value is the same on every machine. `presence`: it adds only whether the variable is set; use it for a secret, or an address that only points at a service.

prerequisites.description: The named prerequisites (scripts/checks/prerequisites.mjs) that the runner makes or verifies before the check runs; `pnpm checks:prepare <name>` makes or verifies one. A check whose prerequisite fails does not run, and its result is `error`. Optional; without it, none.

stochastic.description: true: the result can differ between runs on the same inputs (a model call, a wall-clock bound). A result cache must not reuse such a result, and a reader selects the check only when asked to (it costs model spend or has a wall-clock bound). Optional; without it, false.

cacheable.description: false: a result cache must not reuse the result (the check reads outside state: a base image by tag, a remote state), but a reader selects the check by the normal rules. Optional; without it, true.

intent.description: For an expensive check: what the check catches, and what is never a reason to run it. A reader selects a check without a trace (an eval) by its intent.

tools.description: Eval checks: the MCP tool names that the case declares in its rules. `*` stands for any tool. A reader can select the case when a change reaches code that one of these tools runs (the trace's `tools` edges).
